data.name: Simranraj
data.long_meaning: The name Simranraj is derived from Sanskrit and Punjabi languages. It consists of two words - Simran meaning remembrance of God and Raj meaning king or rule. This name represents the idea of constantly remembering and being devoted to God, as well as having the power and rule to do so. It is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl with a spiritual and devotional personality.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Simranraj was a Jain monk and an influential preacher in 11th century India. The name Simranraj carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Simranraj was born in Gujarat, India, and is known for his teachings on Jainism, particularly on the importance of remembering and repeating the names of the Tirthankaras. He is also referred to as Simhandaswami and Simhaprabhakar. His spiritual influence reached beyond India and extended to Southeast Asia, particularly in the Shwetambar tradition.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Simranraj is found in the 18th century text 'Chandi Charitra', where he is mentioned as a Jain monk who attained a high level of spiritual realization and was revered by the Goddess Kali.
historical_references.context: In this text, Simranraj is described as a Jain monk who lived in the forest and devoted himself to the practice of repetition of the names of God. The Goddess Kali, impressed by his devotion, appeared before him and offered him a boon. Simranraj asked for the power to remember and recite the names of the Tirthankaras at all times. The Goddess granted his wish and blessed him with the ability to remember and repeat the names of the Tirthankaras effortlessly, even in his dreams.
